content: 1. Eslcarbazepine acetate reduces the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction necessitates careful monitoring due to the potential for increased toxicity and the risk of serotonin syndrome. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole, estradiol (including vaginal formulations), estrogens (conjugated synthetic and esterified), and etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised, as coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations of estrogens, increasing toxicity risks. 3. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of estradiol (including vaginal formulations), estrogens (conjugated synthetic and esterified), and etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required to mitigate potential toxicities. 4. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of eszopiclone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, with a reduced starting dose of eszopiclone (1 mg/day) advised. 5. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of ethosuximide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary due to the potential for increased toxicity. 6. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of etoposide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 7. Etrasimod and lopinavir may increase each other's effects via QTc interval prolongation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary due to the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes, especially when coadministered with other QT-prolonging agents. 8. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, etravirine decreases lopinavir levels by the same mechanism. Monitoring is advised. 9. Ritonavir and lopinavir reduce the effects of exenatide (injectable solution and suspension) through mechanisms associated with insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are required, as hyperglycemia has been reported with protease inhibitors. 10. Ritonavir and lopinavir may increase the toxicity of ezogabine via QTc interval prolongation. Monitoring of the QT interval is recommended, particularly when ezogabine is titrated to higher doses (e.g., 1200 mg/day). 11. Fedratinib increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Dose adjustments for CYP2D6 substrates may be necessary, and monitoring is advised. 12. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 14. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 15. Fludrocortisone decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while ritonavir increases fludrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 16. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of flunisolide (inhaled) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 17. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase flurazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification, close monitoring, and consideration of alternative benzodiazepines or dose reduction are recommended. 18. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of fluticasone (furoate and inhaled) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone, necessitating caution and monitoring. 19. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of fluvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Monitoring is required. 20. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 21. Fosamprenavir and ritonavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Fosamprenavir also increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 22. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while lopinavir increases fosaprepitant levels. Monitoring is required. 23. Fosphenytoin decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 24. Fostamatinib increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib's active metabolite). Therapy modification, close monitoring, and dose adjustments may be required. 25. Lopinavir and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is advised, as QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 26. Garlic decreases ritonavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring is necessary. 27. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase gefitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to the risk of adverse effects. 28. Lopinavir and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is required. 29. Ritonavir increases gentamicin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring is advised. 30. Gepirone and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 32. Lopinavir decreases glimepiride effects through mechanisms associated with insulin resistance. Ritonavir may increase or decrease glimepiride levels. Monitoring is necessary, and alternatives should be considered if available. 33. Lopinavir and ritonavir may increase or decrease glipizide levels. Monitoring is required, and alternatives should be considered if available. 34. Lopinavir decreases glyburide effects through mechanisms associated with insulin resistance. Ritonavir may increase or decrease glyburide levels. Monitoring is necessary, and alternatives should be considered if available. 35. Grapefruit increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 36. Griseofulvin decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 37. Ritonavir increases guanfacine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, with a reduced guanfacine dose (half the recommended dose) advised for extended-release formulations. 38. Ritonavir increases haloperidol levels by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is necessary. 39. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase hydrocodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required due to the risk of potentially fatal respiratory depression.
